title: Sudama's handful of rice
hookLine: a poor friend brings Krishna a bundle of flattened rice, and Krishna eats it gladly
carry: offered with love, a leaf is enough for god

cards: A poor brahmin stands at the gates of Krishna's palace in Dvaraka. Tradition calls him Sudama. He and Krishna studied with the same teacher as boys.

Now he's thin, his cloth is worn, and his wife has sent him with the only gift the house could find: a few handfuls of flattened rice, tied in a rag. Inside, everything shines. He's too ashamed to hand it over.
And Krishna, hugging his old friend, asks: what did you bring me?

teach.h: A LEAF, A FLOWER, A FRUIT, WATER.
teach.b: This is from the Bhagavata Purana.

Before Sudama can answer, Krishna says the line he once spoke to Arjuna in the Gita, chapter nine, in paraphrase: whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I accept that offering of love.
Then he pulls the bundle out of his friend's hands and eats a handful of the rice, gladly, and reaches for another, until Queen Rukmini gently stops his hand.
Sudama walks home without having asked for a thing, and finds his hut has become a palace. That's the teaching under every puja, the worship at a home shrine or a temple.
The tray holds a banana, a few marigolds, a tulsi leaf, a little water.

teach.h: GOD ISN'T PAID. GOD IS LOVED.
teach.b: Nothing on it is expensive, and that's the point: God isn't being paid. God is being loved. The verse asks for bhakti, devotion, the love behind the hand.
Then the Gita's next verse widens the tray to hold the whole day: whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer or give, whatever discipline you take on, do it as an offering to me.
So puja doesn't end at the shrine.

teach.h: THE WHOLE YEAR ON THE TRAY.
teach.b: This week we sketched a year of service. On this reading, all of it can go on the tray, small and loved, like a handful of rice.
Tomorrow, the same Krishna, not in a palace but in a dark forest, walked home by someone who loves him.

how: In home and temple puja, Hindus offer simple things such as flowers, fruit, water and tulsi leaves before the deity, and the story of Sudama's flattened rice is widely retold to show that what God wants is the love behind the gift.

o: a festival held once a year at harvest time
a costly ritual that only temple priests may perform
worship: small things like a leaf, offered with love

p: a few handfuls of flattened rice
a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, with love
stops his hand at the next handful

s: Sudama begged Krishna to make him rich
he asked for nothing. he walked home and found his hut had become a palace.
in the Bhagavata, Krishna repeats the Gita's leaf-flower-fruit-water line to Sudama
he says it before he eats the rice.
in the Gita, Krishna asks for costly offerings
he names a leaf, a flower, a fruit and water, offered with devotion.

games.q: you're Sudama at the palace gate with a bundle of flattened rice. everything inside is gold. what does Krishna want from you?
o: nothing at all from a poor man.
games.why: Krishna takes the rice and eats it gladly: whoever offers with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, he accepts.

practice: If there's something small within reach, a leaf, a glass of water, a piece of fruit, hold it in your hands the way Sudama held his bundle; if not, just open them.
Let the year of service you've sketched come to mind piece by piece, the reason, your own service, the gift, the guest, the rhythm, and set each one in your hands.
If you pray, offer it to the one you pray to, the way families set a tulsi leaf or a flower before the home shrine; if not, rest with the weight of it, small and freely given.

wordCard.voice: Puja. Worship at the home shrine or the temple: a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, given with love. Not a payment. A gift.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: patram pushpam phalam toyam, a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, from Gita 9.26.

carryVoice: Your line: offered with love, a leaf is enough for God. Sudama's rice was. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.80–81 (Sudama's visit to Dvaraka; at 10.81.4 Krishna repeats the leaf, flower, fruit and water verse; he eats the flattened rice and Rukmini stops his hand)
Bhagavad Gita 9.26 (a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, offered with devotion)
Bhagavad Gita 9.27 (whatever you do, eat, offer, give, or practice as austerity, do as an offering)
